en: Nora did not go home that night.
She drove to her grandmother's old house.
The place had been sold six years earlier. A young couple lived there now. Nora did not knock. She parked across the street and stayed in the car.
Twenty-eight years ago, she had been five.
What she remembered was pitifully small.
Yellow square tiles in the kitchen.
Her grandmother getting flour all the way to her elbows when she made apple pie.
Her mother's red lipstick, almost never worn.
On November nineteenth, Mara had brought Nora to this house.
A hand pulling the zipper of Nora's coat to her chin.
Her mother crouching down and saying, Tomorrow we're taking the train.
Or had Nora seen two train tickets yesterday and allowed memory to manufacture the sentence?
Journalists were trained to distrust other people's memories.
The rule did not change when the memory was their own.
"You sound like a cheap crime show."
"Then get here before the commercial break."
Elise was already in the Level B2 meeting room.
Three items lay on the table.
Nora opened her phone and found a picture of Mara holding her as a baby.
A narrow silver ring circled Mara's right ring finger.
Martin slid the evidence photograph toward her.
Against a black background lay several metal objects recovered from the fire scene.
"This came from near the body?" Nora asked.
"The original scene number says it was recovered from clothing remains."
"Why wasn't it important in Lena's evidence list?"
"It was listed. 'Silver ring, no evidentiary value.'"
"If her family said it wasn't Lena's, why didn't anyone find out whose it was?"
"Investigators treated it as borrowed property, an old item, or a family identification error."
Nora picked up the insurance attachment.
It listed unassigned items recovered from Warehouse 4 and transferred collectively to police. Beside the silver ring was a note absent from the formal evidence schedule:
The chair legs scraped hard across the floor.
Martin slid the final sheet across the table.
After Mara Bell was reported missing, her family had given police a list of what she might have been carrying that night.
She looked again at the photograph.
The ring lay blackened by fire.
Twenty-eight years earlier, police had classified it as having no evidentiary value because it did not belong to the victim whose identity they had already accepted.
Martin sat across from her with his hands clasped.
"I've requested confirmation from the provincial medical examiner that preserved material still exists for modern DNA testing."
"Who do you think died in that warehouse?"
"I don't have evidence strong enough to make that conclusion."
"I'm not asking what you can put in a report."
Martin looked at her for a long time.
Then he placed Lena Zhou's photograph on the left side of the table.
Between them, the photograph of the fire-blackened ring.
"Twenty-eight years ago," he said, "we asked the wrong first question."
"Now the first question has to be-"
His finger touched the evidence photograph of the body.
"Was the woman in that warehouse Lena at all?"
Nora looked at her mother's young face.
She thought of the two train tickets.
Her mother had intended to take her out of the city.
But Mara never boarded the train.
For twenty-eight years, Nora had assumed her mother went somewhere else.
Now, for the first time, she considered the opposite possibility.
Maybe Mara Bell had never gone anywhere.
Maybe while the entire city spent twenty-eight years looking for her-
she had been here all along.
zh: 诺拉那天晚上没有回家。
她开车去了外婆旧房子。
房子已经卖掉六年，新屋主是一对年轻夫妻。她没有敲门，只把车停在街对面。
她记得的东西少得可怜。
外婆做苹果派时会把面粉弄到手肘。
母亲有一支红色唇膏，几乎从来不用。十一月十九日那天晚上，母亲把她送到这里。
一只手替她拉上外套拉链。
母亲蹲下来，说：“明天我们坐火车。”
还是她今天看见两张车票以后，记忆自己补出来的？
记者最擅长质疑别人的记忆。
轮到自己的时候，规则并不会改变。
第二天上午，Martin给她打电话。
地下二层的会议室里，伊莉丝已经在。
翻到一张母亲抱着婴儿时期的她的照片。
右手无名指上，一只很细的银戒。
黑色背景上放着几件从火灾现场回收的金属物。
“这是从尸体附近找到的？”诺拉问。
“原始现场编号说，是从衣物残留中取出。”
“提了。只写‘silver ring, no evidentiary value’。”
“既然家属说不是她的，为什么没有查这是谁的？”
“当时认为可能是借来的、旧物、或者辨认错误。”
“又一个被故事吸收掉的矛盾。”
诺拉拿起那张保险附件。
上面是一份仓库火灾损失清单，其中记录部分无法归属个人的现场物品被集中交给警方。银戒备注里多了正式证物清单没有的一行：Interior engraving partially legible: N.B. / 1993。
动作太快，椅脚在地面刮出刺耳的声音。
Martin把最后一张纸推到诺拉面前。
是一份1998年的个人物品登记。
Mara Bell失踪后，家属向警方报告她当晚可能携带的物品。
那枚在火里变黑的戒指静静躺在那里。二十八年前，警方把它归类为“没有证据价值”。因为它不属于他们已经认定的死者。
“我已经向省法医中心申请确认当年是否还有可用于现代DNA复检的保存样本。”
“我现在没有证据可以这样下结论。”
然后，他把Lena Zhou的照片放在桌子左侧。把Mara Bell的照片放在右侧。
中间，是那枚烧黑的银戒。
“二十八年前，”他说，“我们问错了第一个问题。”
Martin的手指落在那张尸体证物照片上。
“死在仓库里的，到底是不是她。”
诺拉望着母亲年轻时的脸。
她突然想起两张火车票。
第二天早上八点四十分。
她母亲原本要带她离开这座城市。
二十八年来，诺拉一直以为母亲去了别处。现在第一次，她产生了一个完全相反的念头。
也许玛拉·贝尔哪里都没有去。
也许二十八年前，全城都在寻找她的时候——
在另一个女人的名字下面。
